newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss trade group sees no economic upswing.
newsitem.headline: Swiss trade group sees no economic upswing.

text.p: Swiss trade and industry association Vorort said incoming orders for Swiss companies remained weak and the association anticipated no near-term economic upswing.
The association said it expected domestic consumption to remain weak as the result of rising unemployment and a depressed construction sector.

The outlook for exports was more favourable thanks to improved price competitiveness. But a rapid increase in Swiss export levels could not be expected so long as investment in continental Europe, Switzerland's most important market, is increasing only tentatively.

It further stated that more clarity was needed quickly with regard to reforms in the areas of finance, taxes and social policies with a view toward reducing non-wage costs as a means of improving business conditions in Switzerland.
Earlier this month the economic institute BAK lowered its forecast for 1997 Swiss Gross Domestic Product growth to 1.0 percent from a previous forecast of 1.3 percent.
The Federal Office for Economic Policy is forecasting 0.5 percent (GDP) expansion in 1997. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
